openings.claim: Envelope-specific quantity checklists, marked only after contents enter, move checking into assembly while retaining trays and samples.
openings.discriminator: Checklist benefit with shared trays supports quantity confusion; local loose materials succeeding while correctly used checklists fail defeats that explanation.
openings.probe: Alternate matched-mixture incumbent, shared-tray checklist, and local-material batches; independently count contents, omissions, reaches and all preparation/checking time.
openings.uncertainty: Exact quantities must be available; O4's mixture is unknown. Small-batch success may fail at scale or depletion.

openings.claim: Small same-pattern waves use material passes and a second-volunteer quantity check before closure, reducing adjacent quantity-rule switching.
openings.discriminator: Waves must outperform local-material whole-kit assembly; equal/higher omissions, inadequate space or excess elapsed time defeats the proposal.
openings.probe: Compare equal batches with matched pattern counts; tally preparation, filling, checking, omissions and reaches, then verify a full run if promising.
openings.uncertainty: Useful wave footprint and full-mixture transfer remain unknown.

openings.claim: Pencilled assigned pattern names carry identity through checking and distribution.
openings.discriminator: Marks should survive envelope mixing; separated stacks lose identity when mixed. Contents still need independent checks.
openings.probe: Mark six actual envelopes, verify contents, reorder and recover identity; include marking overhead in full-run timing.
openings.uncertainty: Correct assignments, distinct legible names and affordable overhead are assumptions.

lineage.reason: Quantity/checking and identity relations preserved separately.
Adds mixing discriminator and identity probe.

decision: Probe hypotheses; all evidence is synthetic. Preserve specified quantities/dimensions, exactly two volunteers, at most 90 minutes, the 180-by-75-centimetre table, existing envelopes/supplies and no purchases/equipment. Success requires all 60 ready with at most one distribution correction. Opened-packet footprint, picking-versus-filling errors and depletion despite under-table stock remain unresolved.
